accuracy.evidence: Checked against the England National Curriculum (2013) KS1 English: Year 1 and Year 2 pupils learn to appreciate rhymes and poems, write poetry, and recite some poems by heart with appropriate intonation; and CCSS RL.2.4 (regular beats, alliteration, rhymes and repeated lines supply rhythm and meaning). Rhyme is defined by sound (shared rime), not spelling (high/sky, blue/shoe); every clap count in the lab and items was re-counted by syllable (el-e-phants 3, croc-o-diles snap 4, splash-ing in big mud-dy pud-dles 8, a ti-ny lit-tle grey mouse 7).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips with specific feedback: alliteration taken as rhyme (bus/bell, fish after frog, cake/cook), spelling-based rhyme (blue/shoe, high/sky), one clap per word (elephants, butterfly), clapping letters (butterfly 9), copying a whole earlier line into a pattern poem (I can hear the bees buzz repeated, I like jam), and flat recitation (same-voice prediction, whisper/BANG items). The adult text lists these as common mistakes.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcouplet is a composing lab for ages 6-7: drag a rhyme into the gap of a couplet with the emoji scene, a clap-dot beat matcher that hyphenates the line only after a wrong pick, an I can hear pattern-poem builder that grows a stanza line by line, and a voice picker (loud, soft, fast) that animates the line to fit. It is separate from flagpoem (forms of poetry for 7-10: haiku 5-7-5, narrative, performance) and gate_lab_distinct passes on 6-token shingles.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step asks the child to predict before acting (end sound vs start sound, one clap vs a clap per beat, new end vs copy, same voice vs changing voice), then they do it three times with instant feedback: correct rhymes drop into the gap with a tick, wrong beats show the hyphenated syllables and both clap counts, wrong pattern lines explain whether they broke the start or copied a line. Show me completes each task on desktop and iPhone 13.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each tied to the idea the step then tests: Two words rhyme when they start or end with the same sound; elephants gets one clap or a clap per beat; the next I can hear line starts the same or copies; reading aloud uses one voice or changes to fit the words. The wrong option in each is the real misconception named in the adult text.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Challenge has six fresh items not used in the steps (cake rhyme, butterfly claps, I like jam pattern, whisper mouse, blue and shoe, Big black cat claps). Every wrong choice has its own why() message, for example 9 claps for butterfly says clap the beats, not the letters, and I like jam says that line is already in the poem: same start, new ending.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid explanation FK grade about 0 (target 5.0) with short sentences and words a six-year-old says aloud; adult text FK 10.2 (limit 10.5). The lab uses the young class (big buttons, large tiles), lines of at most seven words, emoji scene cues, and one instruction per screen such as Which word rhymes? Drag it into the gap, or tap it.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a term or a check: rhyme and couplet with bus/fuss, start-vs-end with bus/bell and high/sky, beats with hop hop hop and el-e-phants, pattern and recitation with the I can hear poem. No intro phrases; gate_content passes the filler and similarity checks, and the family tip is a concrete walk activity.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 and desktop 1200x900 in dark and light: tiles and gap stay inside the canvas, the I can hear stanza grows without overlapping the option tiles, and voice cards fit three across. Every drag target has a tappable twin (tap tile then gap), touch targets use the young-size buttons, and the walkthrough logged no console errors.

accessibility.evidence: axe wcag2a, wcag2aa and wcag21aa returned no violations in both themes in the browser gate; the canvas has an aria-label that tell() updates with the current line, gap and result, so a screen reader hears each rhyme and clap result; every action is a real button; colours come from the theme palette and the light-theme screenshot shows dark text on pale tiles.
